summary: Positive observe/reload validation accepts a record whose first initialize response was the tolerated 'Claude API' ambiguity, because only the last verdict is retained.
failure_scenario: OBSERVE with request_writes==1 and AMBIGUOUS_API returns (False, ...) instead of refusing (claude_maintenance_mode.py:_response) and a second initialize is written. Record: request_writes=2, classified_responses=2, mode_verdict='mode-match', refusal_code=None. validate_phase_evidence cannot tell this apart from two matching responses and returns a positive digest, so an API-billing-shaped first observation becomes unreachable in the receipt.
evidence: Read check_claude_phase._mode/validate_phase_evidence (mode_verdict==mode-match, classified==request_writes) against claude_maintenance_mode.py:290-306. The checker's own docstring says the reason describes only the last classified response. Not executed; the tolerance may be intentional, but the positive receipt then asserts more than it retains.

summary: pins() hardcodes active_binding_checked=True and never compares the store's active binding to the identity digest it reports.
failure_scenario: Between assemble() computing provider.identity.store.operator_binding_digest and binding_store.open_candidate(), the active generation is rotated. open_candidate only checks active.key and that the descriptor matches active.json (operator_store.py:1114-1144), not identity.store.operator_binding_digest. pins prints the old operator_binding_digest with active_binding_checked=true, and mint could pin it.
evidence: Read pins() and OperatorStore.open_candidate. The only 'check' is that open_candidate did not raise; the literal True is not derived from a comparison. TOCTOU not executed.

summary: stable_tags requires one complete, unpaginated git/matching-refs listing, but GitHub paginates that endpoint, so the tool either refuses on real data or silently depends on a single page.
failure_scenario: GET /git/matching-refs/tags/rust-v on a repo with more than one page of rust-v tags returns a Link rel=next. fetch() then raises 'is paginated; a listing must be complete', so the bump tool cannot run. The scripted GitHub fake in tests/test_bump_codex_pin.py returns the whole listing in one response and never models this endpoint paginating, so CI cannot detect it.
evidence: Read fetch() (Link check) and stable_tags(); the fake GitHub.__call__ returns the full refs list. No network access here, so the live pagination behaviour of openai/codex is not executed.

summary: Doc claims its source tag rust-v0.153.4 / commit 3d2ee51c is 'the pin the repository cites', but the checked-in workflow pin is rust-v0.160.1.
failure_scenario: A reader relying on the file-and-line citations (manager.rs:2344-2359 etc.) for the S10 refresh run would be reading a vendor version the repo no longer pins. The refresh and failure behaviour cited may differ at 0.160.1.
evidence: grep of .github/workflows/m8-containment.yml:476 shows .../rust-v0.160.1/codex-package-...; tests/vendor_pin.py derives VERSION from that workflow. The document records no re-verification at the current pin.

summary: The proof-inventory test pins only file paths found by a regex, not which tests or selectors run, so the 'two named parity tests' comment is not enforced.
failure_scenario: Step 'Prove containment as the non-sudo service user' lists tests/test_m8_host_runtime.py twice. Replacing the two ::selectors at workflow lines 746-747 with other tests of the same file, or adding -k/--deselect to a step, still satisfies files == inventory.split().
evidence: Read the regex (?:tests/[\w/]+|scripts/check_\w+)\.py and workflow lines 746-747. Only the host-installation and startup steps pin selectors. Not mutated; a removed selector would fail loudly in pytest, so impact is limited to substitution.

summary: mint() writes str(options.journal) and str(options.attempt_record) unresolved and never runs require_coherent, so a relative path mints an authorization that every later run refuses.
failure_scenario: --journal j.sqlite mints a valid-looking authorization; require_coherent then raises on Path(...).is_absolute(). The READ mint (claude_qualification.py:220) behaves the same. It fails closed, but only after the one-time authorization is issued.
evidence: Read mint() and require_coherent() in both entries; tests/api/test_claude_qualification.py::test_wrong_authorization uses 'relative.sqlite' only on the run side. Not executed.

summary: callback_limit=8 is hardcoded in derive_report (and _turn_facts uses 1..8) while pins() reports provider.recipe.call_limit.
